entries.answer: Dugtong means sad or sorry, and it covers sadness and regret as one word where English splits them into several. It is the ordinary word for feeling low, for missing someone and for regretting something, and it is what you say when someone tells bad news. The related word nalLamentaw or kaayo covers pity for someone else, which is a different thing and is often what English speakers mean by sad when describing a third party, so confusing the two is a common learner error. Dugtong is also used with og for a sudden mood, as in naa siya og dugtong, and with a prefix for the lasting state. In a sentence, dili na siya kaayo has become the standard way to say someone has passed away, literally she is no longer well, which is why the phrase appears so often in news.

entries.answer: Kaayo can mean a feeling of happiness, but the word is genuinely ambiguous and the context decides which sense is in play, which is the main thing to know about it. As a mood it means glad or pleased, and as a compliment it means good or fine, and as a noun it means health. The same word also means tired of or fed up when it attaches to a verb, so naa ka na og kaayo is not a compliment but a complaint, and a beginner who reads only the first two letters will get the sense exactly backwards. As a greeting, kaayo is used as a casual stand-in for hello in some regions, particularly in the south, and it is more familiar than the formal kumusta. The polite form kaayo unya is used to a guest and answers a question about how you are doing.
